prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2253 fixes the issue at both ends of the flow: terminate() closes every writer currently registered in self._sse_stream_writers, and streamable_http_manager.py's lifespan is reordered to terminate active sessions before cancelling the task group, which is what actually triggers a graceful close during shutdown. 3218 only adds registration of the GET stream's writer into self._sse_stream_writers inside _handle_get_request; without the manager-side shutdown-sequencing change from 2253, that registration alone doesn't change shutdown behavior, making 3218 a partial subset of the same fix rather than an independent solution.

clusters.pick_reason: #3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the base MCPError class (using MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__ + restoring __dict__), so every current and future subclass gets pickle support for free — its test diff adds `import pickle` and pulls in NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, showing the fix was verified across multiple subclasses. #2555 only adds __reduce__ to UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass (e.g. NoBackChannelError) remains unpicklable and would need its own hand-written __reduce__. #2478 defines a `_restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error)` helper but never wires it into a __reduce__/__reduce_ex__ override anywhere in its diff, and its only other change (dropping a `# pragma: no cover` comment on the `data` property) doesn't alter runtime behavior — so it ships dead code, adds no test coverage, and the pickle TypeError from #2431 is left unfixed.

clusters.pick_reason: 3243 replaces the single lock with two primitives (lock for token-state reads, flow_lock for refresh/authorization transitions), so ordinary resource requests stop blocking on each other once token state is resolved - not just during the final yield. 3252 only moves the trailing `response = yield request` outside the `async with` block, leaving the initialize/refresh/validity-check section fully serialized, and its diff still types the request as httpx2.Request, showing it wasn't rebased past the httpx2->httpx import fix already present in 2779/2858 (merge-conflict risk). 2858's visible diff only reproduces the same httpx2->httpx/import cleanup already done in 2779 (as a rebase of the older external PR 2660); it gives no evidence of a lock-scope change beyond what 3243 implements.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs reject a duplicate in-flight request id before creating its stream entry, but #3063 keys `_request_streams` with `str(message.id)`, which collapses JSON-RPC id `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) into the same key -- reintroducing the exact cross-wiring bug it's meant to fix -- and also leaves a request id equal to the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` string able to collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 replaces this with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct and can't collide with `GET_STREAM_KEY`, covering both edge cases #3063 misses.
